message:
fix MatryoshkaLoss bug: sort sampled dimension indices to maintain descending dimension order (#3203)

When randomly sampling dimension indices for MatryoshkaLoss, ensure they are
processed in ascending order (descending dimension). Previously, when a smaller dimension was be processed
first, the ForwardDecorator would cache the output tensor and then shrink it.
Since the cached tensor and the shrunk output reference the same underlying
memory, the cache would contain truncated embeddings, making them unusable for
subsequent larger dimensions.

subject: Add Sparse Retrieval and Reranking Evaluation with Reciprocal Rank Fusion
message:
Add Sparse Retrieval and Reranking Evaluation with Reciprocal Rank Fusion

- Implemented a new script for evaluating sparse and dense retrieval methods, including reranking and hybrid search using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).
- Added `ReciprocalRankFusionEvaluator` to evaluate hybrid search performance by combining results from dense and sparse retrievers.
- Enhanced existing evaluators (`NanoBEIREvaluator`, `InformationRetrievalEvaluator`, etc.) to support writing predictions to JSONL files.
- Updated the `SparseInformationRetrievalEvaluator` and `SparseNanoBEIREvaluator` to include prediction writing functionality.
- Improved logging and structured output for evaluation results, including detailed metrics for each retrieval method.

subject: Move precision validation before embedding computation (#3385)
message:
Move precision validation before embedding computation (#3385)

* Move precision format validation before training loop

Previously, the code checked if the precision was among the supported options only after the embeddings were computed. If an unsupported format was passed, it would raise a ValueError late in the process, potentially losing all prior work. This commit ensures that precision is validated as a string and among the supported options before any embedding computation begins. This also prevents AttributeError from the .endswith call in quantize_embedding if precision is not a string.

* Check for precision truthy (e.g. accept None), print !r

And modify the tests a bit

subject: [`fix`] `GroupByLabelBatchSampler` to guarantee multi-class batches for triplet losses (#3668)
message:
[`fix`] `GroupByLabelBatchSampler` to guarantee multi-class batches for triplet losses (#3668)

* [`fix`] Replace GroupByLabelBatchSampler with PK sampling + dynamic P scheduling

GroupByLabelBatchSampler produced ~99% single-class batches, causing zero
gradients with Batch*TripletLoss. Replace with PK sampling that guarantees
at least 2 distinct labels with at least 2 samples each per batch.

Dynamic P shrinking reduces P as minority labels are exhausted (down to 2),
improving sample utilization from 9.4% to 99.3% on TREC coarse-like data.
Minority labels (>= 2 samples, < K) get at least 1 scheduled draw into a
proper multi-class batch so they participate in triplet mining.

Fixes #2920

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* Fix GroupByLabelBatchSampler: fallback label columns and reproducible seeding

- Fall back to ("label", "labels") when valid_label_columns is None/empty,
  so standalone construction doesn't crash if the dataset has a label column
- Create a torch.Generator when none is provided, so the seed argument
  always produces deterministic iteration
- Remove redundant tests subsumed by stronger existing ones

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* Refactor sampler with round robin pairs; patches incomplete batches

* Apply my own suggestions

* Use valid_label_columns=["label"] in tests

* Fix __len__/__iter__ mismatch when remainder is 2

__iter__ only yields the final incomplete batch when it has >= 4 samples
(ensuring >= 2 labels with >= 2 samples each), but __len__ counted any
nonzero remainder. When stream_length % batch_size == 2, __len__
overcounted by 1, causing progress bar and LR schedule mismatches.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
